title: Quality Score Calculator
description: The 100-point rubric of validate-sims.py as a checklist in seven groups (main.html 10, metadata.json 30, index.md 35, screenshot 5, lesson plan 10, references 5, p5.js conventions 5), with the script's gates. The score, a 0-100 bar with ticks at 50, 70 and 85, and a colored grade update as checks are ticked. Presets load Bouncing Ball (82), A-star (74) and a blank folder; Suggest cheapest fix highlights the unticked check worth the most points.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Educational Technology
Quality Assurance
MicroSim Engineering

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the quality score and grade of a MicroSim by ticking which rubric checks it satisfies, and will identify the cheapest change that reaches the 85 threshold.
prerequisites: The files of a MicroSim folder and the metadata sections (Chapter 2)
The quality score and rubric table (Chapter 13)

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML elements.

controls.label: One checkbox per rubric check (19) plus "Not a p5.js MicroSim"
Grade letter
controls.action: Show the band table and recommended actions

equations: score = main.html + metadata.json + index.md + screenshot + lesson plan + references + p5.js conventions
assumptions: The rubric and gates are those of validate-sims.py in microsim-utils.
limitations: Invalid JSON in metadata.json (10 points only) and a missing index.md are described, not modeled.

keyQuestions: Which unticked check is worth the most right now?
Why can ticking a check sometimes add nothing?
What else does the gate require besides the score?
commonMisconceptions: The quality score measures learning value.
A score of 85 alone passes the quality gate.
Every check is worth the same, so the order of fixes does not matter.
assessmentOpportunities: Given a list of a MicroSim's issues, the learner computes its score and grade correctly.
The learner names the single change with the largest gain and the fewest changes that reach 85.
